chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The menstruating woman makes up the fasts and does not make up the prayers.

key_terms.تَقْضِي: She makes up (compensates for missed obligations)

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman need to make up her missed prayers?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi delineates the asymmetry in ritual obligations for menstruating women, affirming that while missed fasting is compensable (qada), missed prayers are not, a ruling derived from the understanding that prayer is tied to specific times while fasting is tied to days. This distinction is central to Shia fiqh, distinguishing the nature of salat as a time-bound duty from sawm as a duration-bound one, and is supported by the consensus of the Imams. The ruling underscores the practical ease granted to women during menstruation, exempting them from the rigorous schedule of daily prayers while maintaining the integrity of the monthly fast.

en.hubeali:
Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said:
‘The menstruating woman would make up the (missed) Fasts and would not make up the (missed) Salaats’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from af-Washsha’ from Aban from those who narrated to him has said the foffowing: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said, ‘
Woman experiencing Hayd (menses) must compensatory prayer fasting but not for Salah (prayer).’”
